title: Hom objects into a simplicial semi-representable object turn pushouts of finite simplicial sets into fibre products
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $K$ a simplicial object of the category $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ of semi-representable objects over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object]. Call a simplicial set $S$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] *admissible* if $S_m$ is finite and nonempty for every $m\geq0$ and $S$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices. For admissible $S$ write $H(S)=\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$ with its universal family $(u^S_s)$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object], and for a morphism $f:S\to S'$ of admissible simplicial sets let $f^*:H(S')\to H(S)$ be the unique morphism with $u^S_s\circ f^*=u^{S'}_{f(s)}$ for all simplices $s$ of $S$ (for an inclusion of a simplicial subset this is the restriction morphism). Let $p:A\to B$, $q:A\to C$ be morphisms of simplicial sets and let $D$ with $i:B\to D$, $j:C\to D$ be a pushout of $p$ and $q$ in simplicial sets, with $B$, $C$, $D$ admissible. (a) If $A$ is admissible, then $H(D)$ with $i^*$ and $j^*$ is a fibre product of $p^*:H(B)\to H(A)$ and $q^*:H(C)\to H(A)$ in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$. (b) If $A$ is empty, then $H(D)$ with $i^*$ and $j^*$ is a product of $H(B)$ and $H(C)$ in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$.

proof.text: Assume first that A is admissible. By the finite-limit statement for semi-representable objects, form P = H(B) \times_{H(A)} H(C) in SR(X), with projections r_B:P\to H(B) and r_C:P\to H(C). The maps in the pullback are p^* and q^* from the universal families in the definition of H.

source.place: Lemma 017N (lemma-hom-from-coprod), proof: existence of the required Hom objects and the fibre product

proof.text: For every W in SR(X), a D-family in K over W restricts along i and j to a B-family and a C-family. These restrictions agree after p and q, because i\circ p = j\circ q in the pushout square. Conversely, compatible B- and C-families agreeing after p and q define a unique D-family: in every degree assign a simplex of D its value from either B or C, using the pushout universal property; agreement on A makes this independent of the choice, and the simplicial compatibility equations hold because they hold on B and C. Thus D-families over W are naturally in bijection with pairs of B- and C-families whose restrictions to A agree.

source.place: Lemma 017N (lemma-hom-from-coprod), proof, the displayed sequence of functorial equalities and the final term using the pushout term by term

proof.text: The representing property of H identifies morphisms W\to H(S) with S-families over W, naturally in W. Applying this to S=D,B,C,A and the bijection of the previous step gives a natural bijection between Mor(W,H(D)) and Mor(W,H(B)) \times_{Mor(W,H(A))} Mor(W,H(C)); under it a morphism g is sent to (i^*\circ g,j^*\circ g). The universal property of the categorical fibre product P gives the same bijection with Mor(W,P), with the pair (r_B\circ -,r_C\circ -). By Yoneda (or directly by the representing universal properties), there is a unique isomorphism H(D)\cong P carrying its two projections to i^* and j^*. Hence H(D), i^*, j^* is the asserted fibre product.

source.place: Lemma 017N (lemma-hom-from-coprod), proof, the representing functor equalities and conclusion

proof.text: If A is empty, the compatibility condition in the family bijection is vacuous. The pushout D is the coproduct of B and C, so the same argument gives a natural bijection Mor(W,H(D)) \cong Mor(W,H(B))\times Mor(W,H(C)). Since SR(X) has a final object e and finite limits, this product is the fibre product H(B)\times_e H(C); the resulting comparison isomorphism identifies its projections with i^* and j^*. Therefore H(D) is a product of H(B) and H(C).

split_report.summary: Split the item directly from Stacks Lemma 017N in degree 0. The proof constructs the fibre product in SR(X), identifies D-families with compatible B- and C-families by the pushout universal property in simplicial sets, transports this bijection through the representing universal properties of H(-), and concludes by the fibre-product universal property. The empty-base case is the same argument with a vacuous compatibility condition and the final object, yielding a product. No additional node was needed because all non-elementary categorical structure is supplied by the existing Hom-object, representing-object, simplicial-set, semi-representable, and finite-limits nodes.
